introduction.definition: A firewater monitor is a fixed, swivelling nozzle mounted on a hydrant riser that throws a large stream of water — straight jet for reach or fog for cooling. Oscillating monitors sweep automatically using a water-powered drive so equipment can be cooled without people nearby.
applications: Cooling of tanks, vessels and structures during fires
Process areas, jetties and loading racks
key_points: Jet for reach, fog for cooling

pressure.title: Nozzle pressure sets reach and flow
pressure.description: A monitor delivers a large, aimable flow (≈ 1000–4000 L/min for typical plant monitors) at nozzle pressure ≈ 7 bar. Straight-stream reach can exceed ≈ 40–60 m; fog patterns give a shorter, wider cooling curtain to protect people and equipment from radiant heat. Oscillating monitors sweep automatically so the area can be cooled unattended. Flow ∝ √(pressure): Q = K·√P.

video_tutorials.title: Firewater Monitor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Firewater Monitor.
A firewater monitor is a fixed, swivelling nozzle mounted on a hydrant riser that throws a large stream of water — straight jet for reach or fog for cooling.
Oscillating monitors sweep automatically using a water-powered drive so equipment can be cooled without people nearby.
Typical applications include cooling of tanks, vessels and structures during fires; process areas, jetties and loading racks.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Firewater Monitor works.
Water comes up the riser.
The monitor head swivels and elevates.
The nozzle forms jet or fog.
Water cools the protected equipment.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
A monitor delivers a large, aimable flow (≈ 1000–4000 L/min for typical plant monitors) at nozzle pressure ≈ 7 bar.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Firewater Monitor.
Visual check; drains clear.
Operate through full range; flow test.
Overhaul swivels and nozzle.
Watch for seized swivel: cannot aim. Common cause: corrosion, no exercise.
Watch for short reach: weak stream. Common cause: low pressure, debris in nozzle.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
